newsitem.title: USA: NYC says claims soared, picks accountant for study.
newsitem.headline: NYC says claims soared, picks accountant for study.

text.p: New York City, which in fiscal 1996 paid out nearly $300 million in claims, selected Price Waterhouse to help it cut this expense and make agencies accountable, city officials said on Thursday.

Price Waterhouse will be paid $901,110, to study a range of issues from coordinating the work done by the comptroller and the corporation counsel to analyzing litigation strategies, computer systems, and staffing.

Privatization, which is gaining a foothold in New York City, like other areas in the U.S., also will be considered, along with whether the city should set aside reserves for claims as soon as they are made. One key goal of the study, which was awarded through competitive bidding, is making each agency accountable for the claims that are filed against it.
"They city does not have deep pockets--the claims process needs to be streamlined and the sources of our liability eliminated," said Alan Hevesi, in prepared remarks.
The comptroller noted how rapidly the costs of claims have risen, noting payouts for judgments and settlements have climbed sharply since 1993, when they totaled $247 million.
The city spends around $30 million to $35 million each year for processing and litigating claims.

Saying that more than 11,000 lawsuits are brought against the city each year, the corporation counsel, Paul Crotty, defended the law department's work, saying it "performs admirably. He added "But the enormous increase in the city's payout requires us to search for ways of improving our performance."
